3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: He sighed and slid a report across the table towards me.

4.speaker: Axel Reinhart
4.text: "My security minister woke me up at midnight with this."

5.speaker: Axel Reinhart
5.text: "I was assured that Pales had every right to begin drilling in the Aureus gas field."

6.speaker: Player_Romus
6.text: "Your country sending the drillship was an act of provocation. I had no choice but to respond in kind."

7.speaker: Player_Romus
7.text: "What do you think it means, Your Grace?"

8.speaker: Player_Romus
8.text: "Why did you send that ship to begin with? Why not notify my government?"

9.speaker: Axel Reinhart
9.text: "I was perfectly happy living a life of leisure, coasting off the family fortune, enjoying the odd celebrity rendezvous..."

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: He looked me in the eye.

14.speaker: Axel Reinhart
14.text: "You could have waited for me to state my case. Instead, you proved, once more, that you have no respect for Palesian sovereignty."

15.speaker: Axel Reinhart
15.text: "It means that despite my prior entreaties to you, the Rizian government continues to disrespect Palesian sovereignty."

16.speaker: Player_Romus
16.text: "This is the 'Party Prince' you're talking to. I know the feeling."

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "You didn't have to take his place."

22.speaker: Player_Romus
22.text: "Life is full of surprises, Your Grace. Should we get down to negotiations?"

23.speaker: Axel Reinhart
23.text: "Oh, but I did. Somebody had to step up to protect the Grand Duchy."

27.speaker: Axel Reinhart
27.text: "A brilliant idea, putting jerks like us in charge of entire countries."

28.speaker: Axel Reinhart
28.text: "Yes, I know all about your escapades. In another life, we could've been friends. But in this one..."

32.speaker: Axel Reinhart
32.text: "And who would have stepped up in my stead? Who's left to protect Pales?"

35.speaker: Axel Reinhart
35.text: "You'll have to wait until my memoirs are published. If I live long enough to write them."

36.speaker: Axel Reinhart
36.text: "If I listed them all, we'd never have time for this talk."

37.speaker: Axel Reinhart
37.text: "I'll be honest with you, Your Majesty. I never expected my brother to abdicate."

44.speaker: Axel Reinhart
44.text: "I know that our expedition may have seemed like an act of aggression. But all we are doing is claiming what is rightfully ours."

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: The Duke reached beneath the table and pressed an intercom button.

47.speaker: Axel Reinhart
47.text: "Hilda? Be a doll and help show His Majesty the way out of the building. Wouldn't want him getting lost."

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: He sat back in his chair and scrutinized me closely.

49.speaker: Axel Reinhart
49.text: "My brother always told me never to reason with a Rizian."

50.speaker: Axel Reinhart
50.text: "But what can I say? I'm an optimist."

51.speaker: Player_Romus
51.text: "For the amount I'm paying, something good had better come out of this."

53.speaker: Player_Romus
53.text: "You're lucky that this Rizian sees reason."

54.speaker: Player_Romus
54.text: "You're not your brother. And I'm not my father. We can break this cycle."

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: I rejoined Titus in the reception room. We followed Hilda through winding corridors to the front door.

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: We stepped outside into the waning sunlight. He waited until we were out of the building's shadow to speak.

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: "Surprisingly well. I'm excited to see what comes next."

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "One step closer to Palesian-Rizian reunification, Titus."

62.speaker: Player_Romus
62.text: "The Duke is a snake. But I can still get the upper hand on him."

64.speaker: Player_Romus
64.text: "We may yet have a chance to avenge your father's death."

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: Titus nodded wordlessly. We got into the car and began the long trip back to Porte Drazon.

70.speaker: Narrator
70.text: I hadn't been to Pales in many years.
70.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_MetAxel"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Wehlen_Scapegoats"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Wehlen_Scapegoats"] == true) == false)

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: It was my first visit to Pales since becoming King of Rizia.
71.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_MetAxel"] == true) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Wehlen_Scapegoats"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Diplomacy_Wehlen_Scapegoats"] == true) == false)

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: Titus and I stood side by side, peering out the window of Castle Reinhart.

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: The Grand Duchy's royal residence was built on the foundations of an ancient paleacco, one of the stone fortifications that gave Pales its name.

74.speaker: Narrator
74.text: After his coronation, Duke Axel Reinhart had hired an up-and-coming local architect to expand the old building into a swooping, bulging wood and glass structure that seemed almost alive.

75.speaker: Narrator
75.text: The reception room had been moved to the top floor, and boasted enormous curved windows with a view of the Pales skyline. Its soaring, angular skyscrapers were unlike anything built in Rizia.

76.speaker: Titus Gordion
76.text: "So this is the 'Pearl of the Antacean.'"

78.speaker: Player_Romus
78.text: "Amazing what Lespian money can buy, isn't it?"

79.speaker: Player_Romus
79.text: "Hard to believe all of this sprung up in the last few decades alone."

80.speaker: Titus Gordion
80.text: "I'm a simple man, sir. Give me the classicism of Palas Rezna over... whatever this is."

82.speaker: Titus Gordion
82.text: "'Amazing' is one word for it, sir."

91.speaker: Titus Gordion
91.text: "Your cousin's associates have been less than cooperative. Even if they're innocent in the Wehlen bombing, I suspect they still have something to hide."

97.speaker: Titus Gordion
97.text: "By the way, Your Majesty, the men your cousin turned over have been extradited to Wehlen. There's still no word on what will happen to them."

99.speaker: Titus Gordion
99.text: "Still in the works, sir. It's too sensitive to assign to anyone else, so I'll have to pick it back up once we have significant time in the capital."

104.speaker: Titus Gordion
104.text: "My father was killed during the operation to take back Pales. I took up championship boxing to support my family."

105.speaker: Player_Romus
105.text: "He gave his life for a good cause."

106.speaker: Player_Romus
106.text: "So much senseless bloodshed. May it never happen again."

107.speaker: Player_Romus
107.text: "I bet you were good at it."

108.speaker: Titus Gordion
108.text: "Good enough to get noticed by military recruiters. I do miss those days in the ring sometimes."

109.speaker: Titus Gordion
109.text: "For what it's worth, sir, he believed in the cause. He never turned against King Valero."

110.speaker: Titus Gordion
110.text: "He believed in it with all his heart. He never turned against King Valero."

111.speaker: Player_Romus
111.text: "So you've never been to Pales before?"

112.speaker: Titus Gordion
112.text: "No, sir. My father fought in the operation to take it back. Actually, he was killed here."

113.speaker: Player_Romus
113.text: "Sorry if this visit is bringing up bad memories."

114.speaker: Titus Gordion
114.text: "Not a problem, sir. He died fighting for what he believed in."

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: A panel in the wall slid open, and a secretary clad in a pastel minidress emerged. She motioned for me to enter.

117.speaker: Player_Romus
117.text: "Sit tight. This ought to be quick."

118.speaker: Player_Romus
118.text: "Make yourself comfortable. This might be a while."

121.speaker: Narrator
121.text: The secretary announced my entrance. I stepped into the room and was greeted by Duke Reinhart.

122.speaker: Axel Reinhart
122.text: "Your Majesty. A pleasure to finally meet you."

127.speaker: Player_Romus
127.text: "It's always a pleasure to visit this beautiful castle."

128.speaker: Player_Romus
128.text: "I only wish it was under better circumstances, Your Grace."

129.speaker: Narrator
129.text: The Palesian ruler hadn't aged a day since we last met.

130.speaker: Narrator
130.text: The Palesian ruler was tall and square-jawed, with looks out of an adventure serial. I recalled that the tabloids had nicknamed him "Duke Dashing".

131.speaker: Narrator
131.text: He was tall, square-jawed, with looks out of an adventure serial. I recalled that the tabloids had nicknamed him "Duke Dashing".

137.speaker: Axel Reinhart
137.text: "I thought it best to try and settle this business between ourselves. Like in the old days."

141.speaker: Player_Romus
141.text: "I have to be diplomatic, don't I?"

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: A corner of his mouth turned up.

144.speaker: Axel Reinhart
144.text: "I wasn't sure about it myself. But when you're the leader of such an advanced economy, there's always pressure to keep up with the times. You know how it is."

145.speaker: Narrator
145.text: The secretary left, closing the door behind her. The Duke and I took seats on opposite sides of a wooden conference table.

146.speaker: Narrator
146.text: His posture was casual, even as he regarded me with intensity.

147.speaker: Axel Reinhart
147.text: "And now our ship finds itself in a standoff with the Rizian navy?"

148.speaker: Axel Reinhart
148.text: "Tell me, Your Majesty. What is the meaning of this?"

152.speaker: Axel Reinhart
152.text: "It means that, as usual, the Rizian government continues to disrespect Palesian sovereignty."

153.speaker: Axel Reinhart
153.text: "You could have waited for me to state my case. Instead, you showed that, despite my prior entreaties, Rizia refuses to respect Palesian sovereignty."

154.speaker: Player_Romus
154.text: "I recognize your claim on the field. But you must recognize Rizia's right to it as well."

155.speaker: Player_Romus
155.text: "You broke the law by sending that ship. Count yourself lucky that Rizia has not retaliated."

156.speaker: Player_Romus
156.text: "Rizia does not dispute your claim to the field. In fact, we're prepared to let you keep it."

158.speaker: Narrator
158.text: He raised an eyebrow in suspicion.

162.speaker: Axel Reinhart
162.text: "Is this the same Romus Toras I spoke to three years ago?"

163.speaker: Player_Romus
163.text: "I know our first meeting went badly. This is my attempt to make amends."

164.speaker: Axel Reinhart
164.text: "Let me guess. You want something in return."

165.speaker: Player_Romus
165.text: "My goal has always been to get Pales to rejoin Rizia. If giving up a gas field will help me achieve that goal, I'll do it."

166.speaker: Axel Reinhart
166.text: "You think we're willing to trade our sovereignty for access to natural gas?"

167.speaker: Player_Romus
167.text: "I didn't say I would cede the field out of pure generosity."

168.speaker: Player_Romus
168.text: "My goal has always been to get Pales to rejoin Rizia. If giving up a gas field will help me achieve that goal, I'll do it."

169.speaker: Player_Romus
169.text: "No. I truly don't believe it's worth the hassle to fight for the field."

171.speaker: Axel Reinhart
171.text: "You can't truly think that the field's proximity to Caleqabiz gives you a right to it."

172.speaker: Axel Reinhart
172.text: "Your Majesty, I urge you to let this go. There are more powerful interests at play than either of us."

173.speaker: Axel Reinhart
173.text: "My legal experts have assured me that the proximity of Caleqabiz does not give Rizia a claim to our gas field."

175.speaker: Axel Reinhart
175.text: "You must understand that Pales doesn't owe Rizia anything."

176.speaker: Axel Reinhart
176.text: "By claiming the Aureus field, we are merely asserting the sovereignty that your country has disrespected for so long."

177.speaker: Axel Reinhart
177.text: "Your Majesty, you must understand that Pales doesn't owe Rizia anything."

178.speaker: Player_Romus
178.text: "They supported your independence... by making you dependent on them."

179.speaker: Player_Romus
179.text: "Your family must have realized their motives for doing so were less than pure."

180.speaker: Player_Romus
180.text: "You should never have been put in that position, Your Grace. My predecessors' aggression was out of line."

182.speaker: Player_Romus
182.text: "I see no other choice but arbitration. The Alliance of Nations will decide ownership." [Arbitration]

183.speaker: Player_Romus
183.text: "I suggest you keep the field, and keep the deal with Lespia. Rizia is staying out of this." [Cede Field]

184.speaker: Axel Reinhart
184.text: "Thank you for acknowledging that. But it doesn't change anything."

187.speaker: Narrator
187.text: Duke Reinhart's secretary opened the door. He stood up and gestured for me to do the same.

192.speaker: Axel Reinhart
192.text: "You haven't exactly listened to my government's wishes in the past."

193.speaker: Axel Reinhart
193.text: "You may not have shown hostility towards Pales, Your Majesty, but many in your government have."

194.speaker: Axel Reinhart
194.text: "Sending that ship was our way of asserting Palesian sovereignty."

195.speaker: Player_Romus
195.text: "I hope Rico was right about them not cracking under pressure."

197.speaker: Player_Romus
197.text: "I couldn't care less. I'm sure they're guilty of *something*."

198.speaker: Titus Gordion
198.text: "They're a stubborn lot. My own men couldn't get a word out of them, and believe me, they tried."

199.speaker: Titus Gordion
199.text: "My men did some digging into their backgrounds. Light misdemeanors, mostly."

200.speaker: Titus Gordion
200.text: "I wouldn't feel too sorry for them. Even if they weren't involved in Zille, their record was less than shining."

201.speaker: Titus Gordion
201.text: "We've been making little headway with the Su Omina investigation, by the way."

202.speaker: Titus Gordion
202.text: "Speaking of which, now that our investigation has ended, do you plan to return the Golden Guard to its previous size and function?"

203.speaker: Player_Romus
203.text: "No. The expanded unit might still prove useful."

204.speaker: Player_Romus
204.text: "No. I want all your extra manpower concentrated on that *other* investigation I ordered."

208.speaker: Player_Romus
208.text: "Good point. Yes, that's money I could be putting to better use."

209.speaker: Titus Gordion
209.text: "Right, sir. We'll double down on that one."

210.speaker: Titus Gordion
210.text: "Are you sure, Your Majesty? That would also mean putting an end to the *other* investigation you ordered."

212.speaker: Player_Romus
212.text: "There's too much going on to make this decision. Let's talk later."

216.speaker: Titus Gordion
216.text: "Are you sure, Your Majesty? You never know when you'll need an elite investigation unit at your disposal."

218.speaker: Player_Romus
218.text: "Hmm. All right, let's keep the extra Golden Guards on the royal payroll."

222.speaker: Titus Gordion
222.text: "Very well, Your Majesty. I'll drop the news to the other units when we're back in the capital."

242.speaker: Player_Romus
242.text: "I can only imagine how difficult it must be for you to be here, considering this is where your father lost his life."

243.speaker: Player_Romus
243.text: "There's no doubt in my mind that Pales still falls under the Rizian banner. Their hostile attitude toward reunification is nothing short of a crime."

244.speaker: Player_Romus
244.text: "I do hope our two countries can resolve our historical rivalries. A harmonious partnership could bring significant benefits."

245.speaker: Titus Gordion
245.text: "The pain never really goes away. I've simply learned to live with it."

246.speaker: Titus Gordion
246.text: "Sure. Though I must admit, I do hope to one day see the Rizian flag flying over Pales once more."

247.speaker: Titus Gordion
247.text: "An injustice I hope to see rectified in my lifetime."

251.speaker: Player_Romus
251.text: "I know the feeling. Not a day goes by where I don't think about my late wife."

252.speaker: Player_Romus
252.text: "One mustn't let personal feelings get in the way of doing one's duty."

253.speaker: Player_Romus
253.text: "I got over my wife's death fairly quickly. Granted, she and I were never very close."

254.speaker: Player_Romus
254.text: "As do I. I'm determined to make it happen."

255.speaker: Player_Romus
255.text: "You and me both. Though, this matter must be approached with caution. Setting things in motion takes time."

256.speaker: Titus Gordion
256.text: "Of course. I never meant to imply that it would."

257.speaker: Titus Gordion
257.text: "I've never been married myself, but I can only imagine the heartache one must feel from losing someone so close."

261.speaker: Player_Romus
261.text: "I think about my father on a daily basis too, despite my best efforts to forget about him."

262.speaker: Player_Romus
262.text: "Not a day goes by where I don't think about my own father. I try to remind myself that grief makes one stronger."

263.speaker: Titus Gordion
263.text: "Father-son relationships can be complicated. Everyone's is different."

264.speaker: Titus Gordion
264.text: "An optimistic way to look at life. I admire it."

266.speaker: Titus Gordion
266.text: "Much like a snowflake, grief manifests in countless shapes and forms, never identical."

268.speaker: Player_Romus
268.text: "I believe there are far more pressing issues to deal with than Pales' reunification. It's dangerous when countries try to relive their imperial glory-days."

269.speaker: Titus Gordion
269.text: "While I personally believe the issue is of great importance, I understand your reasoning to give this matter a lower priority."

270.speaker: Narrator
270.text: He maintained eye contact as he bowed to me.

271.speaker: Narrator
271.text: He maintained eye contact as he bowed to me.

272.speaker: Player_Romus
272.text: "This is all a misunderstanding, Duke Reinhart. Send your ship back and we can settle this peacefully."

278.speaker: Axel Reinhart
278.text: "Unfortunately, there are greater interests at play than either of us."

279.speaker: Axel Reinhart
279.text: "I offered you a chance for peace the last time we met. You turned it down."

280.speaker: Player_Romus
280.text: "So you're admitting it. You're a puppet of Lespia."

281.speaker: Player_Romus
281.text: "My own experts would say that you've acted in clear violation of the Alliance of Nations Directive on Offshore Resources."

282.speaker: Narrator
282.text: Duke Reinhart bristled at that remark.

283.speaker: Axel Reinhart
283.text: "Your Majesty, the Reinhart family has ruled over the Palesian peninsula for just as long as the Torases have ruled over Rizia."

284.speaker: Axel Reinhart
284.text: "If you are going to question our legitimacy, you may as well question your own."

285.speaker: Player_Romus
285.text: "That's precisely why I will not let this go. Western superpowers have no place meddling in South Merkopan affairs."

286.speaker: Player_Romus
286.text: "I too have the backing of powerful interests. You do not want to incur the wrath of Rumburg."

287.speaker: Axel Reinhart
287.text: "You are ignoring ANDOR's nuances. It leaves much more room for ambiguity than other laws of its kind."

288.speaker: Player_Romus
288.text: "You ruled on behalf of the Valgos Empire, who stole Pales from Rizia. I would hardly call that 'legitimate'."

289.speaker: Player_Romus
289.text: "I respect the length of your family's rule. However, Pales has only been a sovereign nation for a fraction of that time."

290.speaker: Player_Romus
290.text: "You are correct. Both of our families have clung to power for too long."

291.speaker: Player_Romus
291.text: "Our island counts just as much as your barely legitimate country."

292.speaker: Player_Romus
292.text: "I don't make the rules. Our claim is clearly valid according to the Alliance of Nations Directive on Offshore Resources."

293.speaker: Player_Romus
293.text: "Caleqabiz may be small, but it is still a part of the great nation of Rizia."

294.speaker: Axel Reinhart
294.text: "You chose a convenient time to get patriotic about an island full of exiles."

295.speaker: Player_Romus
295.text: "I was under pressure from my father. I did not truly mean what I said."

299.speaker: Axel Reinhart
299.text: "I offered you a chance for peace three years ago. Instead, you betrayed me to your father."

300.speaker: Axel Reinhart
300.text: "I'm afraid it may be too late for that."

301.speaker: Player_Romus
301.text: "We've established that we have differing interpretations of the law. What will it take to come to a compromise?"

302.speaker: Player_Romus
302.text: "I was under pressure from him then. Now that I am king, I am no longer beholden to his wishes."

303.speaker: Player_Romus
303.text: "I did not and still do not want to cooperate with Pales after the violence of the 1920s. That doesn't mean I want a repeat of that conflict."

304.speaker: Player_Romus
304.text: "I do still have doubts about Pales' legitimacy. But this resource dispute overrides them."

305.speaker: Axel Reinhart
305.text: "But until and unless Rizia respects Palesian sovereignty, we will be forced to assert ourselves."

308.speaker: Axel Reinhart
308.text: "Yes, Pales was part of the Valgos Empire. But we developed our own laws and customs. Even our own language."

309.speaker: Axel Reinhart
309.text: "When the Empire fell apart, what were we supposed to do? Simply give up everything we had built?"

311.speaker: Player_Romus
311.text: "Your family only came to power because the Valgos Empire put you there. And now the Empire is gone."

312.speaker: Player_Romus
312.text: "Your 'sovereignty' only exists because of Lespian support. Without it, Pales would crumble."

313.speaker: Axel Reinhart
313.text: "And what of Rizia and Rumburg? What of the deal your father made with Wehlen to keep House Toras in power?"

315.speaker: Player_Romus
315.text: "Please, Your Grace. Let's not let the hostility between our families color our present relationship."

316.speaker: Player_Romus
316.text: "So you're admitting it. You're a puppet of Lespia."

317.speaker: Player_Romus
317.text: "That's precisely why I will not let this go. Western superpowers have no place meddling in South Merkopan affairs."

318.speaker: Player_Romus
318.text: "I too have the backing of powerful interests. You do not want to incur the wrath of Rumburg."

321.speaker: Axel Reinhart
321.text: "I wish that I could believe you, Your Majesty."

322.speaker: Axel Reinhart
322.text: "Yet I don't see you hanging up your crown."

323.speaker: Axel Reinhart
323.text: "You know, Your Majesty, we Reinharts have ruled Pales for as long as your family has ruled Rizia."

324.speaker: Axel Reinhart
324.text: "That does not mean our sovereignty is undeserving of respect."

325.speaker: Axel Reinhart
325.text: "You are talking about ancient history, Your Majesty."

326.speaker: Player_Romus
326.text: "Pales could have kept its cultural identity intact if it had rejoined Rizia."

329.speaker: Player_Romus
329.text: "I would have done that before turning to Lespia."

330.speaker: Axel Reinhart
330.text: "Your father would never have accepted that."

331.speaker: Axel Reinhart
331.text: "That wasn't your kingdom's decision to make."

335.speaker: Axel Reinhart
335.text: "And your own nationalist tendencies make me think you wouldn't, either."

336.speaker: Axel Reinhart
336.text: "Even if he had, my family never would have agreed. They had too much pride."

337.speaker: Axel Reinhart
337.text: "I heard what it was like back then. Rizia and Morella picking at us like vultures. Goddamn Valgsland trying to provoke a revolution from the sidelines."

338.speaker: Axel Reinhart
338.text: "You don't know what you would have done."

339.speaker: Axel Reinhart
339.text: "Lespia was the only nation willing to support our independence."

340.speaker: Axel Reinhart
340.text: "Of course. But what choice did they have?"

341.speaker: Axel Reinhart
341.text: "You know how wealthy we are. It wasn't entirely a one-way street."

342.speaker: Player_Romus
342.text: "What sovereignty? Your family only came to power because the Valgos Empire put you there. And now the Empire is gone."

343.speaker: Player_Romus
343.text: "Your 'sovereignty' only exists because of Lespian support. Without it, Pales would crumble."

344.speaker: Player_Romus
344.text: "Please, Your Grace. Let's not let the hostility between our families color our present relationship."

345.speaker: Narrator
345.text: He cast a suspicious glance at me.

346.speaker: Axel Reinhart
346.text: "If I must do so to assert Pales' sovereignty, then I will."

349.speaker: Player_Romus
349.text: "Then tell me, how can Rizia satisfy those interests?"

350.speaker: Axel Reinhart
350.text: "I'm afraid it may be too late for that."

351.speaker: Axel Reinhart
351.text: "Lespia, on the other hand, was more than willing to support our independence."

352.speaker: Axel Reinhart
352.text: "But no Rizian ruler has ever truly respected Palesian sovereignty. I don't see why you would be different."

353.speaker: Narrator
353.text: He leaned forward and lowered his voice.

357.speaker: Narrator
357.text: His gaze hardened as he looked at me.

358.speaker: Axel Reinhart
358.text: "No, they won't. They need our gas."

359.speaker: Axel Reinhart
359.text: "I know that. I'm not a fool."

360.speaker: Axel Reinhart
360.text: "But in the meantime, Lespia needs our gas. And they are promising us a sum that we can hardly refuse."

361.speaker: Axel Reinhart
361.text: "So they accepted help from Lespia. The only country willing to support our independence."

363.speaker: Player_Romus
363.text: "Now that Lespia is an ATO member, they won't want to be connected to a monarchy for long. They'll have you overthrown the first chance they get."

364.speaker: Axel Reinhart
364.text: "So you see, Your Majesty, we can't let Rizia take it from us. Not without a fight."

365.speaker: Player_Romus
365.text: "I understand why Pales accepted Lespia's aid. But now that Morella is in league with Valgsland, you could get caught between superpowers."

366.speaker: Player_Romus
366.text: "Let's end the history lecture. What are we doing about this gas field?"

370.speaker: Narrator

694.text: "I am bringing this up so you understand the stakes."

695.speaker: Axel Reinhart
695.text: "We have an obligation to Lespia. When they ask us for natural gas, we can hardly refuse."

696.speaker: Player_Romus
696.text: "Calm down, Your Grace. We have no intention of starting a fight."

697.speaker: Axel Reinhart
697.text: "Then prove it. Send your ships back."

698.speaker: Player_Romus
698.text: "If it's a fight you want, it's a fight you'll get."

699.speaker: Player_Romus
699.text: "You are not the only country with obligations. And the gas field is large enough to be split."

700.speaker: Narrator
700.text: His gaze hardened as he looked at me.

701.speaker: Axel Reinhart
701.text: "I trust Patricio Alvarez more than I trust you."

702.speaker: Player_Romus
702.text: "A compelling argument. But we won't cede the field to you for nothing."

703.speaker: Axel Reinhart
703.text: "Are you sure, Your Majesty? You remember what happened in the 1920s."

704.speaker: Axel Reinhart
704.text: "Sharing a gas field requires close collaboration. You'll excuse me if I don't feel like collaborating with Rizia right now."

705.speaker: Player_Romus
705.text: "I will when you send *your* ship back."

706.speaker: Axel Reinhart
706.text: "Why not? It would avoid us both a lot of headache."

707.speaker: Player_Romus
707.text: "I am considering it. But we have to come to an agreement regarding the gas field first."

708.speaker: Player_Romus
708.text: "How do I know you won't just resume drilling if I call for a retreat?"

709.speaker: Player_Romus
709.text: "Yes. We had you beat until you went crying to Lespia."

710.speaker: Player_Romus
710.text: "Yes. We lost a lot of good men fighting Pales."

711.speaker: Player_Romus
711.text: "I remember better than you. You weren't even born."

712.speaker: Player_Romus
712.text: "I admit I acted harshly. If I agree to call back our ships, can we have a reasonable talk?"

713.speaker: Player_Romus
713.text: "We don't have to collaborate. Just stay on our respective sides."

714.speaker: Player_Romus
714.text: "If you don't choose to collaborate, we will force you to do so."

715.speaker: Axel Reinhart
715.text: "No, I will not withdraw Pales' presence from the field as long as the Rizian navy is there."

716.speaker: Axel Reinhart
716.text: "Excuse me, Your Majesty, but I'm feeling less than agreeable with your ships' guns pointed at mine."

717.speaker: Axel Reinhart
717.text: "If I do that, you can call your ships right back in."

718.speaker: Axel Reinhart
718.text: "Lespia only offered us minor assistance with weapons and equipment. Your own internal strife harmed you more than Lespia did."

720.speaker: Axel Reinhart
720.text: "Then you know how unwise it is to provoke my Grand Duchy."

721.speaker: Axel Reinhart
721.text: "At last, something resembling sanity from the King of Rizia."

722.speaker: Axel Reinhart
722.text: "I am asking you politely. Withdraw your navy, and we will talk."

723.speaker: Axel Reinhart
723.text: "I will give you one chance. Withdraw your navy, and we will have a reasonable discussion about the gas field."

724.speaker: Axel Reinhart
724.text: "There's too much potential for disagreement. Which Rizia has already proved itself incapable of handling."

725.speaker: Axel Reinhart
725.text: "Please, Your Majesty. Neither of us want escalation."

726.speaker: Axel Reinhart
726.text: "Before we continue this conversation, I must insist that you withdraw your navy."

727.speaker: Axel Reinhart
727.text: "Yes. Withdraw your navy, and we will continue this conversation."

728.speaker: Player_Romus
728.text: "Giving in to Pales, and therefore Lespia, would make us look weak internationally. We can't afford that."

729.speaker: Player_Romus
729.text: "Rizia needs the gas in that field, Your Grace. Do not test us."

730.speaker: Player_Romus
730.text: "It's the principle of the thing. I truly believe the field's proximity to Caleqabiz gives us a right to it."

731.speaker: Axel Reinhart
731.text: "And I believe it doesn't. So where does that get us?"

732.speaker: Axel Reinhart
732.text: "Just because you need it doesn't make you entitled to it."

733.speaker: Axel Reinhart
733.text: "Have you thought about how it would make us look to cave in to Rizia?"

734.speaker: Axel Reinhart
734.text: "Please, Your Majesty. We can discuss this. But I want you to withdraw your navy first."

735.speaker: Player_Romus
735.text: "Absolutely not. My ships are staying right where they are."

736.speaker: Player_Romus
736.text: "If it means we can move forward, then fine. I'll call off my ships effective immediately." [Recall Fleet]

737.speaker: Narrator
737.text: Duke Reinhart breathed a shaky sigh of relief.

739.speaker: Narrator
739.text: Duke Reinhart paled. He swallowed before speaking.

741.speaker: Axel Reinhart
741.text: "I see no choice but to call in the AN for arbitration."

742.speaker: Player_Romus
742.text: "Great. They'll easily rule that Pales acted in direct violation of the AN Directive on Offshore Resources."

743.speaker: Axel Reinhart
743.text: "And even if it applies, ANDOR is not black and white. It's very nuanced."

744.speaker: Player_Romus
744.text: "Halaita. If it is said, so it is, so it will be."

745.speaker: Player_Romus
745.text: "It's only nuanced compared to its predecessors. It doesn't stand alone as a brilliant piece of legislation."

746.speaker: Player_Romus
746.text: "We have the support of the international community. Pales doesn't."

747.speaker: Axel Reinhart
747.text: "I never cared for those old Wruhecist saws."

748.speaker: Player_Romus
748.text: "The rules over our maritime borders seem clear to me. And to my councilors as well."

751.speaker: Player_Romus
751.text: "Come on. What happened to solving disputes man to man?"

752.speaker: Axel Reinhart
752.text: "I won't risk it. The potential for inciting an armed conflict is too high."

753.speaker: Player_Romus
753.text: "It's not a saw, it's a promise. Your words shall translate into actions."

755.speaker: Axel Reinhart
755.text: "I'm as God-fearing as the next man. But we can't stay beholden to the words of old saints forever."

757.speaker: Player_Romus
757.text: "Nor do I, but my subjects go crazy for them."

758.speaker: Axel Reinhart
758.text: "Everyone loves a king with a direct line to God."

759.speaker: Axel Reinhart
759.text: "Unfortunately, our options for the Aureus field are still limited."

760.speaker: Axel Reinhart
760.text: "Lespia is on the verge of purchasing the exploration rights to the field. Yet you obviously are not willing to cede it to us."

761.speaker: Axel Reinhart
761.text: "So the only choice I see is to take this to the Alliance of Nations for arbitration."

762.speaker: Player_Romus
762.text: "Wait. If I *do* cede the field to Pales, what will you give Rizia in return?"

763.speaker: Axel Reinhart
763.text: "The chance to avoid a lengthy, costly court process that you will inevitably lose."

764.speaker: Axel Reinhart
764.text: "We don't have much to give, I'm afraid. But maybe Lespia will sell you part of the rights once they've been awarded."

766.speaker: Player_Romus
766.text: "What makes you think Rizia will lose?"

767.speaker: Player_Romus
767.text: "What about a chance for lasting peace between our two nations?"

768.speaker: Axel Reinhart
768.text: "You made it clear that Rizia did not want peace."

769.speaker: Axel Reinhart
769.text: "But if you've changed your mind about that, here's your opportunity to prove it."

770.speaker: Axel Reinhart
770.text: "We have the backing of Lespia, which has the backing of Arcasia. And we both know how much sway the latter has over the AN."

771.speaker: Axel Reinhart
771.text: "But if you'd like to test that theory, be my guest."

772.speaker: Axel Reinhart
772.text: "Well. I can't think of anything else under the circumstances."

773.speaker: Axel Reinhart
773.text: "But even a small percentage of the Aureus field would be a considerable amount of energy."

774.speaker: Player_Romus
774.text: "I refuse to make deals with Lespia."

776.speaker: Axel Reinhart
776.text: "We have the backing of Lespia, which has the backing of Arcasia. And we both know how much sway the latter has over the AN."

777.speaker: Axel Reinhart
777.text: "It's nuanced enough that I believe Pales will get the benefit of the doubt. Especially with international help."

778.speaker: Axel Reinhart
778.text: "Let's see if the AN sees it that way."

779.speaker: Axel Reinhart
779.text: "Remember, we have the backing of Lespia, which has the backing of Arcasia. And we both know how much sway the latter has over the AN."

780.speaker: Player_Romus
780.text: "Your intimidation won't work on me. Remember, my navy is still surrounding your ship."

781.speaker: Player_Romus
781.text: "You're forgetting the support we have from Rumburg and GRACE."

782.speaker: Player_Romus
782.text: "The rest of Southern Merkopa will take my side."

783.speaker: Player_Romus
783.text: "You shouldn't place so much trust in Lespia, Your Grace."

784.speaker: Player_Romus
784.text: "You're right. Calling in a third party will help us find a compromise."

785.speaker: Axel Reinhart
785.text: "In any event, I hope you will send your ships away peacefully once you lose."

786.speaker: Axel Reinhart
786.text: "To the extent that 'compromise' is possible with a kingdom as militant as yours."

787.speaker: Player_Romus
787.text: "Armed conflict... what about arm wrestling? We can settle the argument right here at this table."

788.speaker: Narrator
788.text: He raised an eyebrow. I saw the muscles in his arm twitch.

790.speaker: Axel Reinhart
790.text: "Are you joking? You would lose in an instant."

791.speaker: Axel Reinhart
791.text: "Just as you will lose the arbitration process."

792.speaker: Axel Reinhart
792.text: "I hope you will send your ships away peacefully once you lose."

793.speaker: Axel Reinhart
793.text: "And I hope you will send it away peacefully once you lose."

794.speaker: Player_Romus
794.text: "That's presumptuous of you, Your Grace. You'll find no support from the rest of South Merkopa."

795.speaker: Player_Romus
795.text: "What makes you think we will lose? Remember that we have GRACE on our side."

796.speaker: Axel Reinhart
796.text: "This is the 20th century, Your Majesty. Dying monarchies don't have as much clout as they used to."

797.speaker: Axel Reinhart
797.text: "Will they? After you've shown that you'll deploy your military at the drop of a hat?"

798.speaker: Axel Reinhart
798.text: "And you should not underestimate them. Or us."

799.speaker: Narrator
799.text: He reached under his desk and pressed an intercom button.

800.speaker: Player_Romus
800.text: "That's the only choice? Can't we come to a compromise on our own?"

801.speaker: Player_Romus
801.text: "You're afraid of what would happen if I unleashed the full power of the Rizian military on Pales. As you should be."

803.speaker: Axel Reinhart
803.text: "But if we get into a conflict around the Aureus field, we risk damaging the very resource we're fighting over."

804.speaker: Axel Reinhart
804.text: "Hilda? Be a doll and help show His Majesty the way out of the building. Wouldn't want him getting lost."

805.speaker: Narrator
805.text: He sat back in his chair and scrutinized me closely.

806.speaker: Axel Reinhart
806.text: "You do understand that as long as your navy is in our waters, we are obligated to send our ships to join yours."

809.speaker: Player_Romus
809.text: "I'm sorry that it's come to this, Your Grace."

810.speaker: Player_Romus
810.text: "Watching your face as you surrender will be worth it."

811.speaker: Player_Romus
811.text: "I will respect whatever the AN decides, as long as their judgement is fair and unbiased."

812.speaker: Player_Romus
812.text: "I knew the Duke of Pales would be too cowardly to arm wrestle a real king."

814.speaker: Axel Reinhart
814.text: "This is the 20th century, Your Majesty. Dying monarchies don't have as much clout as they used to."

815.speaker: Axel Reinhart
815.text: "I'll hold you to that, Your Majesty."

817.speaker: Axel Reinhart
817.text: "This entirely avoidable situation? Yes, I'm sorry as well."

818.speaker: Axel Reinhart
818.text: "You do not want to test the strength of the Palesian navy."

820.speaker: Axel Reinhart
820.text: "I truly hope we can come to a peaceful resolution through the Alliance of Nations. For your sake, mostly."

821.speaker: Narrator
821.text: Duke Reinhart's secretary opened the door. He stood up and gestured for me to do the same.

822.speaker: Axel Reinhart
822.text: "I'll see you in court, King Romus."

827.speaker: Player_Romus
827.text: "Then we'll just have to do our fighting elsewhere."

828.speaker: Player_Romus
828.text: "I was only posturing. I have no intention of inciting conflict."

829.speaker: Axel Reinhart
829.text: "I truly hope you don't mean that."

832.speaker: Axel Reinhart
832.text: "With luck, the arbitration proceedings will conclude before mistakes are made."

833.speaker: Axel Reinhart
833.text: "And with more luck, you will send your ships away peacefully when you lose."

835.speaker: Axel Reinhart
835.text: "I am all for arbitration. Just wanted to save you the hassle."

836.speaker: Axel Reinhart
836.text: "Not after your past animosity towards the Grand Duchy. And certainly not after your naval blockade."

840.speaker: Axel Reinhart
840.text: "I'm afraid your naval blockade has precluded any chance of doing business with Pales, Your Majesty."

841.speaker: Player_Romus

849.speaker: Player_Romus

851.text: "You're forgetting the support we have from Rumburg and GRACE."

852.speaker: Axel Reinhart
852.text: "This is the 20th century, Your Majesty. Dying monarchies don't have as much clout as they used to."

853.speaker: Axel Reinhart
853.text: "Will they? After you've shown that you'll deploy your military at the drop of a hat?"

854.speaker: Axel Reinhart
854.text: "And you should not underestimate them. Or us."

855.speaker: Axel Reinhart
855.text: "Let's see if the AN sees it that way."

856.speaker: Axel Reinhart
856.text: "It's not intimidation. I'm just stating the facts."

857.speaker: Axel Reinhart
857.text: "Remember, we have the backing of Lespia, which has the backing of Arcasia. And we both know how much sway the latter has over the AN."

858.speaker: Player_Romus
858.text: "The rest of Southern Merkopa will take my side."

859.speaker: Axel Reinhart
859.text: "Either you cede us the field -- sparing us both a long and costly process -- or we call in the AN."

860.speaker: Axel Reinhart
860.text: "I'm telling you, if you cede the gas field to us without argument, you'll be able to avoid a long and costly process."

861.speaker: Player_Romus
861.text: "I am not backing down. We will have to enter arbitration."

862.speaker: Player_Romus
862.text: "You know what? You're obviously more desperate for this gas field than we are. Keep it if you like." [Cede Field]

870.speaker: Player_Romus
870.text: "It's a small price to pay for a chance at reconciliation."

871.speaker: Player_Romus
871.text: "All I ask in return is that you remember our generosity."

872.speaker: Player_Romus
872.text: "I am hoping that this gives us a chance for cooperation in the future."

873.speaker: Player_Romus
873.text: "You and Lespia will both be first against the wall when the revolution comes, anyway."

874.speaker: Axel Reinhart
874.text: "You sent your navy after us, now you speak of reconciliation?"

875.speaker: Axel Reinhart
875.text: "You sent your navy after us, now you expect us to praise your generosity?"

876.speaker: Axel Reinhart
876.text: "I am glad that you saw reason and backed down. But I do not wish to have any dealings with Rizia in the future."

877.speaker: Narrator
877.text: He reached under his table and pressed an intercom button.

878.speaker: Narrator
878.text: Reinhart reached under his table and pressed an intercom button.

879.speaker: Axel Reinhart
879.text: "You sent your navy after us, and now you speak of cooperation?"

881.speaker: Axel Reinhart
881.text: "Are you serious? If anyone's in danger from the so-called revolution, it's your limping monarchy."

899.speaker: Narrator
899.text: An upfront fee, an annual extraction rights payment, and in exchange, a stable annual energy supply from the gas field.

904.speaker: Axel Reinhart
904.text: "I'm sure you could hold your own in that arena, Your Majesty. But no."

905.speaker: Axel Reinhart
905.text: "We're going to arbitration. And Rizia will lose."

911.speaker: Player_Romus
911.text: "Furthermore, since you were unable to offer us anything, I will not be recalling my fleet after all. Our navy will stay at the field until arbitration is through." [Continue Blockade]

916.speaker: Axel Reinhart
916.text: "I'm sorry it had to come to that."
